runs.final_rubric: Score each candidate 0-10 for predicting y from x1..x5. Strongly prefer exactly two non-overlapping feature pair products with optional linear adjustments (e.g., x1*x3 + x2*x4 - x5). Award perfect scores only for clean multiplicative pairs using all four features exactly once, plus linear terms. Heavily penalize division, abs(), max/min, and any feature reuse across products.

Score each candidate 0-10. Maximize for expressions with exactly two multiplicative pairs (a*b + c*d - e format) using all five features distinctly and linearly. Penalize abs(), max/min, division, nested operations, and triple products. Reward simple additive/subtractive combinations of independent products. Strongly favor the canonical a*b + c*d - e structure. Favor parsimony and interpretability.

Score each candidate 0-10 for predicting y from x1..x5. Strongly prefer exactly two balanced pairwise multiplicative interactions added together (x_i * x_j + x_k * x_l) using exactly 4 distinct features. Heavily penalize: division, conditionals (max/min/abs), subtraction, any third term, asymmetric feature usage, and deviations from the two-product-sum structure.

Score each candidate 0-10 for predicting y from x1..x5. Strongly prefer pure additive/subtractive linear combinations of 2-3 variables—these are optimal and receive 10. Penalize any non-linear operations (multiplication, division, absolute value, max/min, exponents) heavily, scoring 1-2 regardless of linear terms present. Reward simplicity and interpretability.

Score each candidate 0-10 for predicting y from x1..x5. Strongly prefer exactly two independent multiplicative pairs combined additively/subtractively with a single linear term (e.g., x1*x2 + x3*x4 ± x5). Heavily penalize division, conditional logic (min/max/abs), triple products, and asymmetric structures. Favor perfect bilinear symmetry: two balanced pairs plus one linear term only.

Score each candidate 0-10 for predicting y from x1..x5. Strongly prefer exactly two independent pairwise products with no repeated variables across products, combined via addition/subtraction with an optional linear term (e.g., x1*x2 + x3*x4 - x5). Heavily penalize division, max/min/abs, triple products, parenthesized sums in products, and any deviation from this structure.

Score each candidate 0-10 on prediction likelihood. Strongly favor multiplicative numerators with protective min(abs()) denominators plus 1. Reward clean two-feature products in numerators divided by min(abs()) safeguards. Penalize additive numerators, max() operations, nested abs(), and expressions lacking min(abs()) denominators. Prefer simple subtractive final terms over complex combinations.

Score each candidate 0-10 for predicting y from x1..x5. Maximize for exactly two independent pairwise products combined additively/subtractively with optional single-variable linear adjustment (e.g., x1*x2 + x3*x4 ± x5). Strongly penalize abs(), max/min, division, triple products, nested operations, and min/max comparisons. Favor additive/subtractive combination of exactly two bilinear terms with transparent arithmetic.
